packages.name: cli
notes: psc is a thin command router; argument parsing, config/input resolution, compilation pipeline, artifact writing, execution, and each user command are isolated modules.
Root non-workspace gates compile the CLI and execute only dependency-free argument tests; installed CLI smoke belongs to the package-local install/test path.
Implemented commands: init, check, build, run, emit-lean, clean, help, version.
Current psc check/build claim ceiling is the initial reference-backed software subset; theorem/proof declarations are not yet submitted to pskernel.

packages.name: browser
notes: Browser foundation provides cancellation-aware streaming verification through an injected verifier adapter.
Kernel/module WebCrypto wiring remains outside this foundation until the browser-safe module codec is defined.

packages.name: syntax
notes: Declaration parameters preserve Lean BinderInfo categories: default, implicit, strictImplicit, and named instImplicit.
D-EXPLICIT-PARAMS remains a ProofScript-owned non-empty explicit group; native `{...}`, `{{...}}`, and named `[...]` binders remain Lean-shaped syntax.
The function alias still requires at least one D-EXPLICIT-PARAMS group, so native implicit binders alone do not satisfy the alias rule.
Canonical lowering and exact feature-ownership conformance preserve binder categories rather than translating them into TypeScript generics.
Native Lean theorem declarations are parsed as inherited command heads; only registered ProofScript parameter/separator decoration is claimed by feature ownership.
A bounded inherited Lean tactic-term parser recognizes `by exact term` and `by assumption` without registering a new ProofScript syntax exception.
Inherited Lean tactic syntax now includes a bounded `intro name; <continuation>` form; it is not registered as new ProofScript syntax.

packages.name: pretty
notes: Foundation provides compositional documents, width-aware groups/indentation, and diagnostic rendering.

packages.name: meta
notes: Expr metavariables now use pskernel's real Expr and LocalContext rather than only a generic placeholder protocol.
The context records natural/synthetic/syntheticOpaque kind, creation depth, local scope, assignments, recursive instantiation, occurs checks, and kernel-backed validation once assignments are ground.
Ordinary unification never assigns syntheticOpaque metavariables; explicit assignment remains available to tactic/elaboration code.

This is intentionally not full Lean.Meta.isDefEq: level metavariables, delayed assignments, higher-order pattern unification, postponed constraints, local instance synthesis, and transparency-sensitive meta reduction remain later milestones.

packages.name: elab
notes: Lean-native `intro` opens a real forall goal, extends LocalContext with the exact binder type/info, elaborates the continuation against the instantiated codomain, and constructs a lambda proof.
`exact`, `assumption`, and `intro` all elaborate to ordinary pskernel Expr proof terms; Kernel.addTheorem remains final authority.
This milestone still has no synthetic tactic goal engine or cursor snapshots; apply/refine/rewrite/simp/typeclass synthesis and multi-goal tactics remain later work.

packages.name: tactic
notes: Foundation provides generic exact, assumption, and intro state transitions; kernel proof-term construction remains adapter-driven and outside the TCB.

packages.name: compiler-ir
notes: Compiler IR is a distinct typed executable representation lowered from checked software HIR.
IR retains lexical local where declarations explicitly alongside structures, monomorphic inductives, constructors, matches, lambdas, lets, and calls.
Recursive where groups, kernel Expr erasure/lowering, generic ADTs, effects, and optimization passes remain later milestones.

packages.name: runtime
notes: Foundation implements exact bigint Nat/Int basics, saturating Nat subtraction, UInt8 normalization, and tagged constructor values; broader Lean runtime semantics remain later work.

packages.name: backend-ts
notes: Backend accepts only typed executable compiler IR, not raw ProofScript or checked language HIR.
Acyclic where helpers emit as lexically scoped local TypeScript declarations before the containing result expression.
Structures use private unique-symbol brands; inductives use private unique-symbol discriminants and exported constructor objects.
TypeScript Compiler API type-checks generated TS and emits JavaScript, .d.ts, and source maps.

packages.name: language
notes: Software checking has dedicated structure, inductive, match, and where modules rather than one monolithic semantic switch.
Acyclic where helpers are predeclared for local scope, type-checked with outer captures, dependency-sorted, and retained explicitly in checked HIR.
Recursive/mutually recursive where cycles fail closed until Lean-compatible termination elaboration is integrated.
Proof acceptance remains a pskernel/elaborator responsibility outside this software checker.
The executable structure subset accepts explicit named fields only; parsed implicit fields fail closed until generic structure elaboration exists.

packages.name: language-service
notes: Editor analysis distinguishes parse success from kernel verification; only pskernel-admitted declarations are labeled verified.
Declaration-level proof state never fabricates tactic goals: verified theorems report closed, rejected theorems report the actual failure, and unsupported declarations report unavailable.
The service reuses the current parser/elaborator and accepts an environment factory for future project/import integration.
Completion, same-document definition, and reference lookup are lexical/declaration editor aids only; they do not participate in elaboration or kernel admission.
Theorem proof-state responses may include an initialGoal derived from the same real header elaboration used by declaration checking; a verified theorem still reports zero open goals.
Initial goal display is contextual editor information only and is not a cursor-sensitive tactic snapshot.

packages.name: lsp
notes: The stdio LSP reuses the pinned Lean 4.34 Init.Prelude replay fixture to construct a cached pskernel editor environment when available.
Every document analysis receives a clone of that admitted environment; the fixture is replayed by pskernel rather than trusted as pre-verified metadata.
If the fixture is missing or replay fails, the server falls back to an empty environment and reports the degraded editor environment through serverInfo instead of weakening proof acceptance.
Project/import environment composition remains a later language-service milestone.
The transport now exposes completion/definition/references backed by the untrusted language-service index; proof verification status remains independently kernel-derived.

packages.name: project
notes: Foundation provides deterministic dependency ordering, cycle/missing-dependency rejection, and an in-memory build cache; npm/config integration remains later work.
Lean 4.34 final removed deprecated in-kernel native reduction; no NativeEvaluator/native-ir kernel extension is part of the compatibility architecture.
npm workspaces are enabled so package-name imports resolve from the single root install; the root lean-ts-kernel remains the TCB package and outer workspaces may depend on it, never the reverse.
